_: The team size, as a table (docs/modules/solitaire-agile.md, "The team size: who is in the room"). Both halves -- tkTestToolkit -Rituals (Get-P20TeamSize, Get-P20StandupRoomSeats, Invoke-P20StandupFill, Invoke-P20StandupJoinedFill) and Tests/test_rituals.py (team_size, room_seats, fill_standup, fill_joined_standup) -- assert every row. `sizes`: a Space's stored spaces[].features.teamSize in, the room's size out -- a whole JSON number in rituals.teamSizes is itself, anything else (unset, another number, a string, a boolean, a fraction) is rituals.teamSizeDefault -- and `set`, whether the stored value was a size. `seats`: labels only, no engineer -- a room of `size` windows, the chair's one of them, seats size - 1 workers; the workers (in label order) with something to say (not empty) sit first, then the idle, each run in order, and the rest are absent; `present` is the labels present, in the workers' order. `room`: the size is the team -- `size`, the `engineer` ({label, empty}, or null for a fill that has none) and the `labels` ({label, empty}, in label order) in; out, `present` (who sits, in seat order: the engineer, the labels with work, the idle labels), `round` (every speaker in turn order -- the seated, then the invented cast members that fill the seats left -- each with its `label`, whether it is `cast`, and the `window` it sits in: a cast id of consts.json rituals.room.windows) and `desks` (the member windows left empty, in grid order: 9 - size of them whenever the room is full). The stage's seat test is to be this section's third reader. `cases`: a fill end to end with the case's stored teamSize -- the issues fill over `workerLabels`, or, for a case that states `cards`, the joined fill over its own `labels`, `issues` and `cards` for `space`/`spaceName`: the response's team.size, every worker of the record kept with its empty and present, the `round` (work.workers: each speaker's label, name and cast, in turn order), and the three renderings against their goldens byte for byte -- the detail and the brief (the record: every worker, never an invented one) and the work (the round). Goldens are generated by Tests/regenerate_joined_goldens.py, never typed.
